$comment: The extract engine's coercion-target vocabulary (FieldKind), pinned across ports.
This is the machine-readable form of the `kind` values documented in README.md ->
'schema.json field keys'. Every port's extract engine runs the same corpus, so a port
that quietly adds or drops a kind changes what that corpus can even express.
It was unpinned until now, and it had already drifted: C# carries a Decimal kind that
no other port has and no fixture exercises. Nothing failed, because nothing looked.
Gated by scripts/check-extract-field-kinds.mjs in ci-local.sh's `gates` lane.
$kotlinNote: Kotlin ships no extract engine of its own — metadata-ktx drives the shared Java one, so there is no Kotlin FieldKind to check and adding one would itself be the drift.

reason: C#'s extract engine coerces a field.decimal to a native `decimal` through this kind,
and MetaObjects.Render's ExtractMap.AsDecimal reads it. It is NOT dead vocabulary.
It is a deviation rather than the canonical shape because the outcome it buys does not
require an engine kind: Java reaches the same place (a typed BigDecimal on the response
record) by leaving the engine's STRING coercion alone and converting in GENERATED code.
That keeps the engine's vocabulary small and puts the port's native-type choice at the
port boundary, which is where ADR-0019 says it belongs.
Not removed here because removal is not the one-line change it looks like: AsDecimal has
no string arm, so an engine that stopped producing `decimal` would make it return null
for EVERY decimal — silently. Reconciling properly means either propagating DECIMAL to
the other four engines or moving C# onto the generated-coercion pattern, and either is a
cross-port behaviour change that wants its own spec.
This entry exists so the divergence is a reviewed decision with a stated cost, not an
accident nobody can see. Anything NOT listed here fails the gate.
